title: ArrayList and Wrapper Types
summary: The growable ArrayList - adding, getting, setting, removing, searching and sorting - the List interface, wrapper classes like Integer and Double, autoboxing and its traps (remove by index or value, == on Integers, null unboxing), List.of, and iterating while removing safely.

cards.a:
Generic collections hold objects only; use the wrapper type `List<Integer>`

Collections hold objects, not primitives. Each primitive has a wrapper class, and autoboxing converts between `int` and `Integer` for you.

The item at index 1

With an `int` argument, `remove` picks the by-index version. To remove the value 1, call `list.remove(Integer.valueOf(1))`.

cards.q: What happens when you call `add` on `List.of(1, 2)`?
cards.a:
`UnsupportedOperationException` is thrown

`List.of` returns an unmodifiable list. It compiles, because the type is still `List`, but changing it fails at run time; copy it with `new ArrayList<>(...)` to get a list you can change.
